findings: Requirements doc (booking cancellation) contains zero mention of refunds, payment, or money — only status change and slot release are specified — yet both implementations move money via refund(booking.payment), meaning the refund policy was invented ad hoc in each codebase rather than derived from any spec.

The two 'cancel a booking' implementations enforce contradictory refund policies for the same operation: api/cancelBooking.ts (customer self-service) withholds refund when hoursUntil(booking.start) <= 24, while admin/cancelBooking.ts (support staff) calls refund(booking.payment) unconditionally regardless of timing — same action, two different financial outcomes depending on who performs it.

Because admin-initiated cancellation always refunds, the 24-hour cutoff enforced on the customer path is trivially bypassable: a customer who cancels late through the self-service UI is denied a refund, but the same customer contacting support to cancel the same booking gets a full refund — the policy is effectively optional and dependent on which channel is used, not a real rule.

The 24-hour refund threshold ('hoursUntil(booking.start) > 24') is a hardcoded magic number that exists only inside api/cancelBooking.ts's code — it is not stated anywhere in the requirements doc, is not configurable, and its exact boundary behavior (a booking exactly 24 hours out) is defined only implicitly by the '>' comparison.

Neither cancelBooking nor adminCancelBooking checks the booking's current status before acting; calling either function again on an already-cancelled booking re-runs releaseSlot and refund unguarded, so a duplicate request (double-click, client retry, race between concurrent requests) would trigger a duplicate refund with no idempotency protection.

Both implementations perform status update, slot release, and refund as three unguarded sequential statements with no transaction, rollback, or error handling shown; if refund() fails partway through, the booking is left marked 'cancelled' with its slot already released but no refund issued, and nothing in the shown code detects or reconciles that mismatch.

There is no logging or audit trail distinguishing an admin-issued refund override from standard policy enforcement, so after the fact there is no way to tell whether a given admin refund on a late cancellation was a deliberate, authorized exception to the 24-hour policy or simply the unconditional behavior of admin/cancelBooking.ts firing by default.
